findings.title: Curve-bias 'at most 0.5 K per week' is false: 0.6 K in a 7-day window
findings.claim: docs/ecl110.md:31, configuration.md:767 and how-it-works.md:1152 say the learned heat-curve bias moves at most 0.5 K per week, but CurveLearner lowers it by 0.6 K within 7 days on consecutive comfortable days.
findings.mechanism: _step_down caps each 0.2 K step by 0.5 x (days since the last step)/7, i.e. against the previous step only; steps come every 3 comfortable days, so three steps (0.6 K) fit in any 7-day window.

evidence.unit: K (largest bias drop over any 7-day window in 70 comfortable days; RESULT curve_bias_max_7day_drop_k)
evidence.machine: cloud container, 4 CPU, Linux (box B2, shared)
evidence.contention_note: fan-out: other finder seats on the same 4-CPU box; counts only, contention-immune

findings.metric_definition: max over d of bias(day d-7) - bias(day d) while CurveLearner.record_day is fed one comfortable day (margin 1.0 K) per calendar day for 70 days
findings.phenomenon_property: The learned curve bias never falls by more than the documented weekly figure over any 7-day window, and every document stating that figure states the same number.
findings.seam_rule: grep -rnE '0\.5 K per week|half a degree per week|≤0\.5 K per week' docs README.md custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/strings.json custom_components/heatpump_optimizer/translations

null_control.note: with the per-step cap scaled to 0.3 K/week the same 70-day drive stays under 0.5 K, so the harness separates the two

findings.proposed_fix_scope: Either restate the docs (0.2 K per three comfortable days, about 0.47 K/week on average, up to 0.6 K in 7 days) or make _step_down cap the drop over a trailing 7-day window; the seam rule lists every copy of the figure.

findings.title: how-it-works.md: space solve 'from two starting points'; it runs four, each refined and polished
findings.claim: docs/how-it-works.md:108-113 says the space solve runs from two candidate initial guesses and a third start was not worth doubling the runtime, but a real solve passes four candidates to _multi_start_minimize and runs 8 L-BFGS-B minimizations.
findings.mechanism: _solve_space builds [guess, price-ranked, half-headroom, low-energy price-ranked] on the initial solve and _multi_start_minimize refines every candidate and polishes each (#1208); _warm_start_starts adds the previous plan as a fifth after the first cycle (read, not measured).

evidence.unit: starting candidates in the first multi-start call (RESULT space_solve_start_candidates; space_solve_minimize_calls=8)
evidence.machine: cloud container, 4 CPU, Linux (box B2, shared)
evidence.contention_note: fan-out: other finder seats on the same 4-CPU box; counts only, contention-immune

perturbation.change: --perturb-starts: truncate each multi-start call to its first two candidates

findings.metric_definition: len(candidates) handed to optimizer._multi_start_minimize on the first space solve of tests/stress.py:build_case(season='winter', two_zone=False, dhw=False)
findings.phenomenon_property: The number of starting points and refinements how-it-works.md states for the space solve equals what optimizer._multi_start_minimize receives and runs in a real solve.
findings.seam_rule: grep -rnE 'starting point|initial guess|third start|multi-start' docs README.md
findings.proposed_fix_scope: Rewrite the 'Two starting points, not one' paragraph to the current four structural seeds plus the previous-plan candidate, each refined and polished; drop or re-measure the 2.2 %/0.2 % figures.
